rationale: C09 plausibly supplied a material template for the child: both are presidential letters supporting voluntary civilian efforts on behalf of armed-forces personnel, explain why public participation is important, and culminate in confidence that informed Americans will respond. The child's statement that informed countrymen will support the campaign closely parallels C09's assertion that once Americans know the facts they can be counted on to respond. C08 has a related appeal for public support of a voluntary organization serving military personnel, while C16 supplies mobilization-era calls for citizens to sacrifice for national welfare, but neither matches the child's structure as closely as C09.

shared_material.child_excerpt: If our countrymen are informed of these needs, I am sure they will subscribe and oversubscribe the campaign goal.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Once the American people know the facts, they can be counted on to respond with vigor, determination, and eventual success.
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive parallel prediction that informing the American public will produce the desired voluntary response.

shared_material.child_excerpt: how vital the success of this campaign is to the welfare of our armed services and to our people
shared_material.parent_excerpt: efforts ... to stimulate community organization on behalf of the men and women of our armed forces
shared_material.explanation: Both frame civilian voluntary action as directly supporting the welfare of armed-forces personnel.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I urge my fellow Americans to give generously and promptly
shared_material.parent_excerpt: all sections of the community join these programs
shared_material.explanation: Both conclude the substantive appeal by calling broadly for civilian participation in a voluntary support effort.
